header.running_head: Enduring Hunger when Inviting People Towards Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ

blocks.text: each person two dates. He then said to them, "Eat these two dates and drink some water. It will suffice for you for the day."

Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) says that he ate one date and kept the other in his lower garment. Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "O Abu Hurayra! Why have you kept that date away?" Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) replied, "I have kept it for my mother." "Eat it," said Rasulullaah ﷺ, "I shall give you two dates for her as well." Rasulullaah ﷺ then gave him another two dates.[^1]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ went to the trench (before the Battle of Ahzaab) early one morning, he found the Muhaajireen and Ansaar digging in the cold because they had no slaves to do the work for them. When he saw the fatigue and hunger they were suffering, he said:

"O Allaah! There is no life but the life of the Aakhirah
Do forgive the Ansaar and the Muhaajirah (the Muhaajireen)"
In response to this, the Sahabah (RA) said:

blocks.arabic_text:
نَحْنُ الَّذِيْنَ بَايَعُوْا مُحَمَّدًا
عَلَى الْجِهَادِ مَا بَقِيْنَا أَبَدًا
blocks.text:
"We are those who have pledged allegiance to Muhammad
Pledged to wage Jihaad as long as we are alive"
Another narration from Hadhrat Anas (RA) states that as the Muhaajireen and Ansaar dug the trench around Madinah and carried the sand on their backs, they sang:

blocks.arabic_text:
نَحْنُ الَّذِيْنَ بَايَعُوْا مُحَمَّدًا
عَلَى الْإِسْلَامِ مَا بَقِيْنَا أَبَدًا
blocks.text:
"We are those who have pledged allegiance to Muhammad
Pledged to wage Jihaad as long as we are alive"
In response to this, Rasulullaah ﷺ would say:

"O Allaah! There is no real good but the good of the Aakhirah
Do bless the Ansaar and the Muhaajirah (the Muhaajireen)"

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates further that even when two handfuls of barley was brought, it was cooked with decaying fat and served to people who were extremely hungry (and ate it) even though it would not go down easily and had an unpleasant odour.[^2]

Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "As we were digging the trench for the Battle of Khandaq a very hard large boulder got in our way. We went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, 'This large boulder in the trench has come in the way. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'I shall come down (to see).' As Rasulullaah ﷺ stood up, (we noticed that) he had a stone tied to his stomach and we had not as much as tasted any food for three days." The Hadith continues in detail.[^3]
